messages:
Maya: Heads-up — saw a P95 latency spike right after the continuous-batching heuristic change at ~1893456720. p95 jumped from 110ms -> 320ms for short-chat workloads.
Sam: Yea, I'm seeing a ~25-30% throughput drop on the rgx-gpu pool. Small requests are getting fragmented into odd microbatches.
Jin: I captured kernel-selection logs and a couple of flamegraphs. Initial clue: kernel selector flipped from fast_fused_attn to fallback_attn_fp16 for a lot of batches.
Maya: paste of selector snippet:
```
[selector] model=redwood-1-v2, batch_shape=(3,128), avg_tokens=9.1 -> choose=fallback_attn_fp16 reason=batch_shape_variance>threshold
[perf] expected kernel=fused_attn_fp16 est_ms=1.2 chosen_ms=3.8
```
Sam: Also noticed KV cache hit-rate for the same traces dropped from ~92% to ~76% after the change. Could be causing more cold prefixes and smaller effective batch sizes.
Priya: The heuristic tweak lowered token_budget_target for small-req lanes from 8 -> 6 to reduce latency tail in high-load sims. Might be overconstraining merge windows.
Leo: Ah — reducing token budget increases the chance of starved batches that are non-uniform shapes. That explains the kernel selector switching to a safer but slower kernel that handles ragged shapes.
perf-bot: :warning: perf-alert: p95 latency increased by 2.9x on pool=rgx-gpu; affected routes: /chat/stream, /complete/small. Links: https://perf.redwood/p/1893456
Jin: I ran local ncu on the failing trace; stack shows significantly more memcpy and kernel launches. nvlink activity elevated. Likely more KV movement between stages due to cache misses.
Sam: Quick repro command I used: `PYTHONPATH=./tools python -m loadtest.synthetic --profile small-chat --qps 200 --seed 42` — reproduces within 2m.
Maya: Proposed mitigation: revert token_budget_target change for small-req lanes and add a guard in selector to prefer fused_attn if >70% batches match {seq<160, batch>=4} shape. Thoughts?
Priya: I support rollback to get p95 back while we iterate on selector. Also will add telemetry: emit batch_shape histogram to perf service so we can reason statistically.
Leo: I'll run A/B canary with rollback on 5% capacity and synthetic traffic to validate.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy scheduled by Maya for rollback config: rollout_id=rbk-189345-1 target=rgx-gpu percent=5 — starts in 10m.
Jin: Longer-term fix: change kernel selector scoring to use batch_shape_distribution over last 60s instead of instantaneous variance; and make token_budget_target aware of KV cache hit-rate. I sketched pseudo: 
```
score(fused_attn) = w1*expected_latency + w2*(p(batch_shape in fused_fast_shapes)) - w3*kv_miss_penalty
```
Sam: Add regression test: synthetic mix with 70% short prompts, vary token_budget from 4..12 and assert fused_attn selection ratio >= 0.7 for stable perf.
Maya: Good. Action items: 1) rollback token_budget_target for small lane (Priya) 2) canary and validate (Leo/Sam) 3) add batch_shape telemetry (Priya) 4) implement selector scoring change RFC (Jin) 5) perf tests (Sam). I'll follow up once canary results in. :thumbsup:
Leo: Running the canary now, will post numbers in this thread.
Maya: Thanks — please include p50/p95/p99 and kernel-selection breakdown (counts) per minute.
Sam: If rollback shows no regressions I can schedule a hotfix patch.
Jin: Also saving the capture (nvprof and flamegraph) under /var/artifacts/perf/1893456789 for later triage.
Maya: Great. Keeping this thread open until canary completes.
